scenario: AITA for not hosting thanksgiving like I planned to | For about 50 years, my mom hosted all of her children and grandchildren for thanksgiving and Christmas Eve. She’s now gotten too old and asked us kids to take over the tradition. There are 4 of us so we just rotate. We’ve each hosted one holiday so far. This thanksgiving is my turn. We have never spent thanksgiving or Christmas Eve with my wife’s family. We’ve just never been as close to them plus they live all over the country. Well this year her mom and aunts decided to go to the Macy’s thanksgiving day parade. At first it was just a sister’s trip but then they decided to invite all their kids and grandkids to meet them up there. My wife really wants to go. She hasnt seen some of her aunts and cousins in years. Our daughter wants to go because it’s a “once in a lifetime event” (which i agree with). And I want to go. As soon as we decided to go I called my older brother to see what we should do about thanksgiving because I can’t host this year. He said our oldest sister is going to be pissed and i have to tell her myself. He wished me luck. So I call her and she is mad. She says she’ll probably have to end up hosting even though she is up next for Christmas and I’m being inconsiderate of what our mom asked us to do. “Mom wouldn’t abandon thanksgiving to go to nyc” and went on about how sad mom will be that I’m doing this. I offered to pay for them to rent a spot and have it catered but she said that takes away from the close knit family vibe. My brother said his wife might be up for it but he didn’t sound too happy about asking her. My other sister can’t do it because she’s renovating her house. I do feel bad for backing out of my turn but I tried to offer up solutions and I also offered to host the next holiday—which my oldest sister said no to because it’s her turn and she’s been planning for it all year. Next up is my brother so I said me and him could maybe just swap thanksgivings if his wife is up for it. Am I in the wrong here?

It's the person's turn this year, but they want to go to the Macy's parade with their wife's family. They called their older brother to see what to do, and the brother said the oldest sister would be mad. The sister was indeed upset, saying she might have to host, which is her turn for Christmas, and that the mom would be sad. The person offered to pay for a rental and catering but the sister didn't like that idea. The brother's wife might help, but he wasn't happy about it. The other sister can't host because she's renovating. The person offered to host the next holiday but the sister refused, saying she's been planning it. The person suggested swapping with the brother if his wife is okay. So, is the person in the wrong here? I think the key points are: 1. The tradition was established by the mom, and the siblings agreed to rotate hosting. The person's turn is this year, so they have a responsibility to host. 2. The person wants to go to the parade with their wife's family, which is a once-in-a-lifetime event for their daughter. That's a valid reason, but it conflicts with their family obligation. 3. They tried to find solutions: offered to pay for a rental and catering, which the sister rejected because it changes the family vibe. They also offered to host the next holiday, but the sister refused. 4. The brother's wife might help, but the brother isn't happy about it. The other sister can't host. So, the person is trying to balance family obligations with personal desires. They did reach out to their siblings and tried to find alternatives, which shows they care about the family tradition. However, the sister is upset because it's her turn next, and she's been planning for it. The person's offer to host the next holiday was refused, so that doesn't solve the problem. I think the person isn't entirely in the wrong because they're facing a difficult situation and tried to find solutions. However, they might have been more considerate of the sister's feelings and the family tradition. Maybe they could have communicated better or found another way to make it work without making the sister feel like she's being forced to host again. But ultimately, they did try to offer solutions, so I don't think they're the asshole. It's a tough spot, and both sides have valid points.
